font_files: video/resolve/assets/fonts/hetrixotypeface-extrabold.otf — 'Hetrixo Typeface ExtraBold' / PS HetrixoTypeface-ExtraBold. UPM 1000, weight 800, 335 glyphs, GSUB=none, GPOS=kern. capHeight 660, xHeight 507, digits 670, asc 1000 / desc -400 / lineGap 0 (hhea == OS/2 typo). Full Latin-1 + Latin-Ext (a-tilde, c-cedilla, o-acute all present), plus U+00D7 x, U+2013 en-dash, U+2014 em-dash, U+2026 ellipsis, U+00B0 degree, U+2030 permille. NO 'tnum' feature and no GSUB at all: figures are PROPORTIONAL — '1' is 0.325 em but '0' is 0.667 em (2.05x). Any live counter/timer MUST use fixed per-digit slots, not the natural advance.

video/resolve/assets/fonts/fontspring-demo-alvitonovacomp-bold.otf — 'FSP DEMO - Alvito Nova Comp Bold'. UPM 1000, weight 900, only 96 glyphs, GSUB=ccmp/frac/locl, GPOS=kern. capHeight 732, xHeight 445, hhea asc 900 / desc -300 / lineGap 100, winAscent 1149. Charset is U+0020-U+007E ONLY: zero accents, zero x/en-dash, zero ellipsis, zero degree. And it is UPRIGHT, not italic: post.italicAngle = 0.0 and the measured stem centroid shifts only -10/-2/+8 units over 732 units of height for l/H/I (i.e. vertical).

video/resolve/assets/fonts/fontspring-demo-alvitonovacomp-bolditalic.otf — same family and same 96-glyph ASCII-only DEMO subset, but italicAngle -22.0 and a real slant (stem centroid shift +127 units over 732 units of height = ~10 deg of visual lean). If the 'cursive accent' is supposed to read as cursive/italic, this is the file that delivers it; the filename named in the brief does not. Use one of the two deliberately, do not silently mix.

Loading note: the existing scaffold (edit/motion-v2/src/kit/fonts.tsx) already loads both brief-named files through @remotion/fonts with a delayRender gate and family names 'Hetrixo'/'Alvito'. Keep the gate — the whole typographic contract dies if headless Chrome photographs the system fallback. Fallback stacks in that file (Helvetica Neue / Georgia) should never appear in a frame.

type_scale.name: heroNumber
type_scale.use: u13 '5-18x' (546 px wide, leaves 187 px each side of the 920 content column), u08 '94%' (454 px @208 -> 506 px @232), u14 '0,50', u03 bar value. Digit ink height = 0.670 em = 155 px; '%' matches digits exactly (0..670 units) so it needs no nudge. Digit advances differ wildly (0.325-0.667 em): for a ticking value render each digit in its own fixed 0.70 em slot (162.4 px) and centre the glyph in it, otherwise the string crawls sideways. Baseline anchor: with lineHeight L and size S, cap-top is at (L-1.4S)/2 + 0.34S from the box top; at L=S that is 0.14*S = 32.5 px. Ink bottom of '0,50' is the comma at -0.094 em = 21.8 px below the baseline — budget for it when bottom-aligning.

type_scale.name: heroLabel
type_scale.use: The word that names the hero, one per beat: 'SIM' / 'NAO' in u03 (product labels, set them at equal optical weight, do NOT let either win by size), 'mais rapido' in u13, the model name in u08. Cap height 47.5 px — 1/3 the hero number's, which is the ratio that reads as 'label for this number' rather than 'second headline'. Baseline anchor: 0.14*S = 10.1 px from box top at lineHeight=1.

type_scale.name: cardTitle
type_scale.use: The card's own name in u09/u10/u11 ('inbox', 'chamado', 'fatura'). These three beats are the same stage with a swapped card, so the title must be the same size in all three — the personality comes from the card's interior (rows, bars, stamp), never from the title size. Cap height 37.0 px.

type_scale.name: chipValue
type_scale.use: The percentage inside a decision chip: 94%, 4%, 2% in u01, the rising value in u08. Digit ink height 34.8 px. Right-aligned on the chip's inner right edge so the decimal column is stable while the number grows. Colour = ink #1C1A18 on a cream chip, cream #F4EFE6 on an ink chip; never gold at this size on cream (1.61:1).

type_scale.name: chipLabel
type_scale.use: The word inside a chip: 'financeiro', 'suporte', 'humano' (u01), 'financeiro / suporte / urgente / humano' (u07). Cap height 22.4 px. Lowercase, no tracking, left-aligned on the chip's inner left edge. At 34 px 'financeiro' is 157 px wide — that is 2.5 columns of the 62 px grid, so a chip needs 4 columns (296 px) to hold label + value with a 32 px gutter.

type_scale.name: smallCaps
type_scale.use: Uppercase, letter-spacing +0.14 em (3.4 px) — the eyebrow/section label: CLASSIFICA, ENCAMINHA, CHECA, ESCOLHE (u09-u12), MODELO (u12), and any 'what this card is' tag. This is the only role that gets tracking; nothing else in the system is letterspaced. Cap height 15.8 px. Colour muted #5A544E on cream (6.52:1) — this is the one place muted is legal. Minimum legal size in the whole system; below 24 px Hetrixo's strokes start to shimmer at 1080p.

type_scale.font: Alvito Nova Comp Bold (see font_files — this file is upright; use -bolditalic.otf if it must lean)
type_scale.name: accent
type_scale.use: ONE per beat, never two: the cursive/condensed contrast voice — the single accented word under a hero (e.g. the payoff word under '5-18x' in u13). Cap height 45.4 px, so it optically matches a 69 px Hetrixo — i.e. this 62 px Alvito sits visually between chipValue and heroLabel, which is why it can carry an accent without becoming a second headline. HARD CONSTRAINT: the DEMO subset is ASCII-only, so the accent word can contain no accents — 'mais rapido' with an o-acute renders tofu. Pick ASCII-safe accent words ('mais rapido' -> 'na hora', 'de graca' -> 'setup', 'inbox', 'SIM'). Gold is the intended colour but ONLY if the accent sits on an ink plate or is drawn as a shape; gold on cream is 1.61:1.

type_scale.name: unit
type_scale.use: The unit/suffix that rides with a hero number but must not compete with it: the 's' in u14's '0,50 s', the 'x' in u13 if you decide to break the multiplier off, '%' in u08. Set at 0.38x the hero number, on the same baseline, with a 0.18 em space (42 px) before it. Cap height 58.1 px.

type_scale.name: logoCaption
type_scale.use: The small line under a brand mark when the mark alone is ambiguous — u04 (JEV), u05 (ChatGPT), u12 (the chosen model), and the small ChatGPT context mark in u13. Cap height 19.8 px. Muted #5A544E on cream, ink on a tinted badge. Never place it inside the mark's own bounding box; the marks in this kit are full-bleed with no internal padding.

type_scale.name: microLabel
type_scale.use: The absolute floor of the scale: unit glyphs inline with chipLabel ('%' on a secondary chip), axis ticks on the u03/u08 probability bar, and the row labels inside the u09/u10/u11 cards. Anything smaller than 20 px is not legible on a phone at 1080x1920 and should be deleted rather than shrunk.

palette.name: cream
palette.use: Palco C full frame (opaque). Palco B: NEVER as a full-frame fill — below y=960 every pixel must be alpha 0 and the cream comes from the separate hostB bake. On palco B cream is only legal as the fill of a small plate or as the ink colour reversed out of an ink badge. 15.15:1 vs ink, 6.52:1 vs muted.

palette.name: ink
palette.use: All primary type and all plate fills that must read as solid. 15.15:1 on cream. This is the workhorse: on a cream canvas an INK plate with cream type is the strongest and most 'premium product' move available, and it is the direct fix for the current ugly white chips — a white plate on cream is only 1.15:1, so the plate has no edge at all and relies entirely on its shadow (that is exactly why the current u01_B reads as 'chip branco estatico'). Also the tint target for the off-palette brand marks (see assets_recon).

palette.name: muted
palette.use: Secondary type only, and only on cream: 6.52:1 there. NEVER on an ink plate (2.32:1, unreadable). Its legal jobs: the smallCaps eyebrow, the logoCaption, the tick labels on a probability bar, and the un-selected state of a chip. It is not a plate colour and not a shadow colour.

palette.name: gold
palette.use: Accent only, and only in three shapes: (a) as a FILLED shape with ink type on it — ink-on-gold is 9.40:1; (b) as TYPE on an ink plate — 9.40:1; (c) as a 2-6 px underline/rule/underline-sweep under an ink label on cream. It is 1.61:1 against cream, so gold text or a thin gold hairline on the cream canvas is a decoration you cannot see — that is a bug, not a subtlety. Gold never touches white (1.85:1) and never carries body copy. Budget: gold appears in at most one element per beat.

palette.name: white
palette.use: Legal ONLY on ink (17.35:1) — reversed type on an ink badge or plate, and the 1 px highlight on the top edge of an ink plate. It is 1.15:1 against cream, i.e. invisible; a white plate on the cream canvas is the exact defect being fixed, so white is never a plate fill on palco C and never a type colour on cream.

palette.name: ALPHA.hairline  rgba(28,26,24,0.14)
palette.use: Derived, not a new colour: the 1 px (at 1080) hairline that gives a cream plate on a cream canvas an edge. Use it instead of white/black borders. 2 px if the plate is larger than 6 columns.

palette.name: ALPHA.plateLift  rgba(28,26,24,0.16) / ALPHA.plateShadow rgba(28,26,24,0.10)
palette.use: Derived: the two-step elevation. plateShadow (0 18px 44px) on resting plates, plateLift (0 30px 70px) on the plate that is currently the hero of the beat. Ink-tinted, never neutral grey and never a coloured glow — a coloured glow is what makes motion graphics look like a template.

palette.name: ALPHA.track rgba(28,26,24,0.08)
palette.use: Derived: the empty track of every progress/probability bar (u01 fill bars, u03 SIM/NAO bar, u08 probability). The filled portion is ink or gold; the track is ink at 8%. Never a grey hex.

palette.name: BANNED outside the 5
palette.use: The teal ChatGPT squircle (2.30:1 on cream) and the #D97757 Claude starburst (2.73:1 on cream) are the only chroma in the asset kit and both fight the palette at those ratios. Either tint both to ink #1C1A18 (recommended, 15.15:1, mark stays 100% recognisable) or move them onto an ink plate (teal 6.59:1, coral 5.56:1). No third option: raw teal/coral on a cream canvas breaks the 'sem chroma' rule and reads weak. Also banned on principle: every derived colour made by tinting gold or muted toward each other — derive only with alpha on the 5.

grid:
GRID — 12 columns, exact fit to the brief's margins. Frame 1080x1920. Margin 80 left / 80 right => content 920 px, x = 80..1000 (identical on palco B and palco C). 12 columns of 62 px with 16 px gutters: 12*62 + 11*16 = 744 + 176 = 920, exact, no rounding. Column left edges: n=1..12 at x = 80 + 78*(n-1) => 80, 158, 236, 314, 392, 470, 548, 626, 704, 782, 860, 938 (last column 938..1000). The frame centre 540 lands exactly on the midpoint of the col6/col7 gutter (532..548), which is the proof the grid is correctly centred — any layout that puts a column edge at 540 is off-grid. Column spans: 3 cols = 218 px, 4 = 296, 5 = 374, 6 = 452, 8 = 608, 12 = 920. Default component widths: chip = 4 cols (296), card = 12 cols (920), brand badge = 5 cols (374), half-canvas block = 6 cols (452). Note 920 also factors as 12*40 + 11*40 and as 16*50 + 15*8 if a different rhythm is ever wanted, but 62/16 is the one to lock.

SPACING SCALE — base 8 px, all gaps are multiples of 8: 8, 16, 24, 32, 40, 48, 56, 64, 80, 96, 112, 128, 160, 192, 240, 320. The only 4 px step allowed is an optical nudge (see the x-sign nudge below). Named roles: pad-inside-chip = 32 h / 24 v; gap-between-chips = 16; gap between a plate and its caption = 12 (the single legal non-8 value, it is an optical attach); section gap = 40; group gap = 64.

VERTICAL ZONES — Palco B overlay (graphics only, alpha 0 below y=960): top safety 40; eyebrow band 88..152 with the smallCaps cap-top at 96; graphic field 152..664; hard floor for opaque pixels = 700 at EVERY frame INCLUDING the drift and the enter overshoot (the enter travels down and the drift adds -5 px on y, so author the resting bottom at 664 to leave 36 px of headroom); reserved caption band 700..960 stays empty — do not put a hairline, a rule or a fading element there, a caption agent owns it. Palco C (opaque cream): top safety 80; eyebrow 120..168; hero field 200..1240; hard content floor 1400; reserved caption band 1500..1750; 1750..1920 stays empty for platform UI. Both stages: keep the same left edge (80) for every text block so cuts between B and C do not shift the type.

VERTICAL RHYTHM — a Hetrixo line at lineHeight L and size S places its cap-top at (L - 1.4*S)/2 + 0.34*S from the top of its box, because hhea gives asc 1000 / desc -400 / gap 0. At lineHeight = S that is 0.14*S. So to put a cap-top on a grid line Y, set the box top to Y - 0.14*S (e.g. smallCaps 24 -> offset 3.4 px; heroNumber 232 -> offset 32.5 px). For Alvito the multipliers are different (hhea asc 900 / desc -300): cap-top = (L - 1.2*S)/2 + 0.168*S, i.e. 0.068*S at lineHeight = S. Because two different metric conventions are in play (hhea vs OS/2 winAscent 1149 for Alvito), calibrate each family ONCE by rendering a probe glyph and measuring the cap-top, then store the two offsets as tokens — do not compute them per beat from theory.

OPTICAL NUDGES (measured, not guessed): U+00D7 'x' in Hetrixo has ink 149..470 units = its visual centre sits 22 units (0.022 em) ABOVE the digits' centre at 330-335, so it must be pushed DOWN by 0.022*S px (at 232 px that is 5.1 px). It is also small (0.321 em tall vs 0.670 em digits), so set the multiplication sign at 1.30x the number's size (302 px when the digits are 232) or it reads as a speck. U+2013 en-dash is already optically centred (285..376, centre 330.5) — no nudge. The comma descends to -94 units: when bottom-aligning '0,50' against a grid line, the ink bottom is the comma, 0.094 em below the baseline.
assets_recon: jev/logo.png — 400x400 RGBA, ink bbox (97,50)-(302,349) = 206x300 px (aspect 0.687), 27,906 opaque px = 17.4% of the canvas, ONE connected component. It is a monogram/ornamental letterform (an interlocking ligature-flourish built from uniform-thickness strokes), NOT a disc and NOT a wordmark. Alpha is hard-edged: zero pixels between alpha 20 and 200, so it was quantised/downscaled and carries NO anti-aliasing — it will look crunchy if pushed much past 300 px tall, so cap it there. Colours: #171717 is 94.8% of the ink, then #402237, #773263, #963B7B totalling 1,465 px = 5.2% of the ink — a real magenta/maroon fringe riding part of the contour. PLACEMENT: use it as-is on cream for u04 (contrast 15.65:1, reads as ink); the fringe is invisible at video scale. Never put it on an ink plate (1.03:1, it disappears). If the fringe bothers you, do NOT redraw it: reload the PNG and repaint every pixel with alpha>0 to a flat #1C1A18, which is a three-line PIL op and loses nothing.

jev/wordmark.png — DO NOT USE. 1024x1024 RGBA but it is not a wordmark: there are no letterforms in it. Its content is a stack of full-width horizontal colour bands (blue #3866A6, rust #8F4A31, black #1A1A1A/#000000, light grey #E4E4E4) with a solid opaque bar 27 px tall spanning the entire 1024 px width at y=0..26, a single vertical seam at x=608, and the band pattern roughly repeating about x=512 (mean |delta| 26.6 per channel, so not even a clean mirror). Connected-component analysis returns 201 pieces, the large ones being 294x53 rectangles at x=13..306 (y=161, 225, 289, 353, 417, 481...), i.e. a block mosaic. Content stops at y=682. Ink coverage 33.8%. Colours #E4E4E4 31.2%, #1A1A1A 22.9%, #1E1E1E 8.8%, #8F4A31 6.7%, #3866A6 5.4%, #000000 3.5%. Verdict: broken raster. This is also moot because the brief for u04 explicitly wants 'mark JEV, nao wordmark de texto' — so u04 should use jev/logo.png. The vector source jev/wordmark.svg is the real wordmark, but it is itself multi-coloured (#000 x99, #1E1E1E x57, #FEFEFE x24, #3866A6 blue x16, #8F4A31 rust x16, #3B9033 green x4) and would inject blue/rust/green into a five-colour piece. Recommendation: neither file goes on the canvas.

chatgpt/logo.png — 1024x1024 RGBA, alpha bbox = the ENTIRE canvas (full bleed, no padding anywhere), 782,234 opaque px = 74.6% ink, 8 connected components. Shape (confirmed from logo.svg, viewBox 0 0 2406 2406): the OpenAI app-icon SQUIRCLE, not a disc — corner radius 577/2406 = 0.24 of the side on the top-left, top-right and bottom-left corners, with a SHARP bottom-right corner. Fill is teal #74AA9C = 98.6% of the opaque pixels. The OpenAI knot inside it is fully TRANSPARENT in this PNG (the SVG paints it white; the raster has it knocked out), so at rest the knot shows whatever is behind — on palco C that is cream. Contrast teal-on-cream = 2.30:1, weak, and it is one of only two chroma sources in the kit. PLACEMENT, in order: (a) recommended — tint the whole badge to ink #1C1A18 (alpha as the mask); you get an ink squircle with a cream knot, 15.15:1, fully on-palette, and it is still unmistakably the OpenAI mark; (b) if the teal must survive, sit it on an ink plate where it reads 6.59:1; (c) raw teal on cream only if you consciously accept one chroma accent. Sizing: because it is full-bleed and has a sharp corner, at S px it eats the whole SxS box — reserve the box, do not add padding inside it. Recommend 5 cols (374 px) for u05 and 112 px for the small context badge in u13.

claude/logo.png — 1024x1024 RGBA, alpha bbox (0,0)-(1022,1023) = the ENTIRE canvas (full bleed, no padding), 420,685 opaque px = 40.1% ink, exactly ONE connected component. Shape (from logo.svg, viewBox 0 0 100 100): the Claude/Anthropic STARBURST — a many-rayed irregular asterisk whose rays run all the way out to the edges of the box. Not a disc, not a wordmark. Fill #D97757 = 97.7% of the opaque pixels (the SVG declares hsl(14.8, 63.1%, 59.6%), the same colour). Contrast coral-on-cream = 2.73:1 — too weak for a shape this big on cream, and it is the second chroma source. PLACEMENT: tint to ink #1C1A18 for the cream canvas (15.15:1) — a bold single-colour starburst reads beautifully as ink; or keep coral only on an ink plate (5.56:1). Because the rays touch all four edges at S px, add your own optical padding: place the ink inside a box 1.4x the size you want the mark to appear, or the rays will look cropped. Relevant beat: u12 (ChatGPT / Claude / Grok chips).

grok/logo.png — 1024x1024 RGBA, alpha bbox (50,0)-(973,1023) = 924x1024 px (aspect 0.902), 445,303 opaque px = 42.5% ink, and EXACTLY 4 disconnected components — which matches the four <polygon>s in its source (viewBox 0 0 466.04 516.93, the xAI slashed mark: a big parallelogram, a bottom-left triangle, a top-right wedge and a full-height right bar). It is a MARK, not a wordmark; it is full-bleed vertically (y=0..1023) and has 50 px of side bearing. Fill is pure #000000 = 98.4% of the opaque pixels. Contrast black-on-cream = 18.34:1 — the strongest mark in the kit, and it already reads as ink. PLACEMENT: keep it AS-IS on cream; it needs no tint. Never put it on an ink plate (1.21:1, it vanishes). Reserve a 0.90-aspect box (e.g. 5 cols = 374 wide x 416 tall). Optional consistency move: repaint #000000 -> #1C1A18 so all three marks are literally the same ink; on cream you cannot see the 18.34 vs 15.15 difference and it makes the kit one system. Relevant beat: u12.

KIT SUMMARY (the honest one): of the four logos, only TWO are already in the cream/ink/gold palette — grok (pure black, 18.34:1) and jev/logo.png (#171717, 15.65:1). The other two are chroma and both are too weak on cream — chatgpt is a teal #74AA9C squircle at 2.30:1 and claude is a #D97757 starburst at 2.73:1. The single highest-leverage decision in this whole spec: tint chatgpt and claude to ink #1C1A18 via their alpha channel, and the entire canvas becomes one ink-and-cream system with gold as the only accent. That one op removes every colour conflict without redrawing a single asset. And jev/wordmark.png is a broken raster that must never be placed.

PLATE-STACKING NOTE for brand marks on cream: because grok and jev are near-black and chatgpt/claude (tinted) are ink, a cream plate under a mark is invisible (1.15:1 white-on-cream, and a cream-on-cream plate has literally zero edge). So either put the mark straight on the cream canvas with a generous 40 px margin and let the shape carry itself, or put it on an INK plate with the knot/mark reversed out to cream. The in-between — a mark on a faint grey card — is exactly the 'static white chip' look the brief is replacing.
risks: The file the brief names as the cursive/italic accent (fontspring-demo-alvitonovacomp-bold.otf) is UPRIGHT, not italic: post.italicAngle = 0.0 and its stems are measurably vertical. The true slanted cut is fontspring-demo-alvitonovacomp-bolditalic.otf in the same folder (italicAngle -22.0, ~10 deg visual lean). Decide this once, explicitly, and load only the chosen file — if the accent is meant to read as handwriting, the named file will not deliver it and the 'accent' role collapses into 'a second condensed bold', which is not a contrast.

Alvito is a 96-glyph DEMO with charset U+0020-U+007E ONLY. Any accented character in the accent word renders as a fallback or tofu: 'mais rapido' with an o-acute is unsafe, 'de graca' with a c-cedilla is unsafe, 'SIM'/'inbox'/'setup'/'na hora'/'18x' are safe. Because the accent is a single designed word per beat, this is easy to miss until the render shows a hole. Hetrixo is safe for anything (full Latin-1 + Latin-Ext).

Hetrixo has NO 'tnum' feature (no GSUB table at all): figures are proportional, and '1' is 0.325 em while '0' is 0.667 em, a 2.05x spread. A timer or counter that advances naturally will crawl horizontally — u14 (0,50 s) and u08 (~94 rising) are both exposed. Render each digit in a fixed 0.70 em slot, centred, or the whole beat looks broken. This is the single most likely visual bug in the piece.

Gold #F4B400 is 1.61:1 against cream. Any gold text, gold hairline or gold 1-2 px rule placed directly on the cream canvas is effectively invisible and will read as a rendering error rather than a subtlety. Gold is legal only as a filled shape with ink type on it (9.40:1), as type on an ink plate (9.40:1), or as a 2-6 px underline under an ink label. Conversely muted #5A544E is 6.52:1 on cream but 2.32:1 on an ink plate — the two derived colours have opposite rules and swapping them is an easy mistake.

A white plate on the cream canvas is 1.15:1: no edge at all, defined only by its drop shadow. The current PIL overlays are exactly this (u01_B samples as a field of #F0F0F0 chips on cream), which is the literal cause of the 'chip branco estatico' complaint. On palco B the fix must be structural: hero plate = ink fill with cream type, secondary plates = cream fill with the 1 px rgba(28,26,24,0.14) hairline. White is a type colour for ink plates only.

Palco B's hard rule (every pixel below y=960 must be alpha 0, graphics confined to y=40..700) collides with the required continuous entrance-plus-drift spline. The drift adds -5 px on y and the entrance travel is up to 26 px, so an element authored to rest at y=700 will cross the 700 line during its own motion, and an ink plate resting at 700 will have its shadow below it. Author the resting ink bottom at 664 and keep every shadow/blur within the element's own box, or the alpha-0 check on the rendered PNG will fail on the frames where the motion is moving.

chatgpt/logo.png and claude/logo.png are FULL-BLEED with zero internal padding (ink bbox equals the whole 1024 canvas) — chatgpt's squircle even has one sharp bottom-right corner. Placing either at S px produces a mark that touches all four edges of its box, so any layout that assumes padding will look cropped, and any plate sized to the mark's visible silhouette will be wrong. Reserve the full box and add spacing outside it.

Both the ChatGPT badge and the Claude starburst are large-area chroma at low contrast on cream (2.30:1 and 2.73:1). If they are left untinted they become the loudest thing in the frame (big area beats contrast in the size > contrast > colour > position hierarchy) while also being the least legible — the worst of both. Tint to ink or place on an ink plate; there is no third option that survives the 'sem chroma' palette rule.

Two different font-metric conventions are in play (Hetrixo: hhea asc 1000/desc -400/gap 0; Alvito: hhea 900/-300 with +100 lineGap and winAscent 1149). Cap-top offsets computed from theory will be wrong for one of the two families depending on whether the renderer reads hhea or OS/2 winAscent. Calibrate each family once with a probe render and freeze the offset as a token, rather than deriving it per beat — otherwise Alvito accents will sit a few px off their Hetrixo partners and it will look like sloppiness rather than a bug.

The JEV identity has a second, unrelated vector family in the kit (jev/mark.svg, jev/wordmark.svg) that is a deliberately multi-coloured pixel/rect design (blue #3866A6, rust #8F4A31, green #3B9033). It is tempting as a 'wordmark' source, but rendering it injects three colours that are not in the palette into a five-colour piece, and its raster (wordmark.png) is broken anyway. Keep the JEV presence to the monogram only.
